title: 8 free qualitative data analysis software tools compared
summary: See what free qualitative data analysis software really covers. We compare 8 tools on free version limits, video support, collaboration, and security.
body_markdown:
Is there free qualitative data analysis software? +


Yes. Several tools offer software for qualitative data analysis free of charge. Some are open-source programs you download and install, some run online in a browser, and some paid platforms have a free plan with limits on projects or seats. Before installation, check which operating systems the tool supports, and look on its website to see whether the free version allows commercial use.


Is QDA software hard to learn? +


It depends on the tool. Simple tools that cover the basic functions, like highlighting text and adding a basic code, can take under an hour to pick up. Full desktop packages with more menus and analysis options have a steeper learning curve and can take several days. If you need something user-friendly, try it on a few real transcripts before you commit.


Can you use a spreadsheet for qualitative data analysis? +


Yes, for small projects. You paste quotes into rows, add a column for each code and filter to compare answers. It gets hard to manage on complex projects with many interviews or codes that change partway through, and a spreadsheet can’t link a quote back to the recording.


Can QDA software handle quantitative data and mixed methods projects? +


Some can. Several QDA tools let you attach demographic or survey data to each participant, so you can compare how different groups talked about a theme. For statistical analysis, you’ll usually export the coded data to other tools. Conveo can also ask rating and multiple-choice questions inside the interview, so the quantitative answer and the reason behind it come from the same person.


Is free QDA software safe for sensitive data? +


Desktop programs keep files on your own computer, so data doesn’t go to anyone else’s server. Hosted versions of free tools often don’t say where data is stored or how it’s protected. Open-source tools also vary in how actively they’re developed, so check for regular updates before you rely on one for sensitive qualitative research.


Can AI code qualitative data for you? +


AI can suggest themes, apply your codes across interviews and summarize what came up, which saves time on large studies. AI working from transcripts alone can miss sarcasm or hesitation, so a researcher should still check the coding before findings go into a report.
